text_blocks.snippet: The permanent shutdown of AT&T's email-to-text gateway (@txt.att.net) has broken legacy messaging workflows across many libraries. Because major carriers like Verizon and T-Mobile are also phasing out or strictly filtering free email gateways, migrating away from the SMS::Send::Email driver is critical.
To restore patron texts in Koha, you have three primary architectural paths depending on your library’s technical resources, budget, and support structure.
1. Direct API Driver Integration (Recommended for Self-Hosted or Vendor-Supported)

Instead of relying on email protocols, Koha can talk directly to commercial SMS gateways via API. This bypasses carrier email blocks entirely, satisfies modern 10-DLC (Ten-Digit Long Code) compliance rules, and provides real-time delivery tracking.

table: Change SMSSendDriver preference to Twilio or deploy the ByWater Interactive Twilio Plugin.
Very low per-message cost; robust open-source library support; supports interactive replies (patrons text keywords to renew items).
Requires setting up an independent Twilio account, configuring a 10-DLC campaign brand, and normalizing patron phone numbers to E.164 format (+1XXXXXXXXXX ).
Choose another carrier-approved aggregator via MetaCPAN (e.g., SMS::Send::Us::Ipipi).

text_blocks.snippet: 2. Turnkey Third-Party Library Integration (Easiest / Fully Managed)
If you prefer not to manage API accounts, compliance registration, or phone number formatting, you can route Koha data through specialized third-party library notification services.

text_blocks.snippet: If you want a fix that requires zero configuration changes inside Koha's notification preferences or patron database, you can use a commercial middleware service.

list.snippet: How it works: You subscribe to a service like TextBolt or . They give you a unique routing domain. You change your Koha "Cellular Providers" email gateway to point to their domain instead of AT&T's. Their servers receive your ILS emails, strip the wrapper, and push them natively to mobile networks through registered A2P channels.
Pros: Highly convenient. No need to clear out or modify old patron "Provider" fields or rewrite notices.
Cons: Continues reliance on an aging architectural concept (routing SMS through email forms) rather than shifting to a true native system API framework.
